uncertainty_budget.explanation: The Indian market price of the token against the official rupee rate for a dollar. This is the bulk of the gap and it is the part everyone argues about.
No rate was published on the settlement date. Stepping back to 2026-06-25 or forward to 2026-06-29 is undetermined — Rule 206 does not say which.
A daily candle is not a price. It is a range with four printed readings and no rule choosing between them.
The retrieved pair is USDT/INR. The receipt was USDC. The figure is USDT/INR x USDC/USDT, and treating the peg as exactly 1.0000 is a further choice.

regimes.outcome: The receipt is classified as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset, taxed at 30% under s.115BBH. The recognition date is the date of transfer. The valuation method is the price that the virtual digital asset would ordinarily fetch on sale in the open market on the valuation date. TDS is applicable at 1% if the payer is a resident. Penalty position is governed by s.439(8), requiring disclosure of all material facts and a bona fide explanation.
regimes.reasoning: The classification of the receipt as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset is directly governed by s.115BBH, which imposes a 30% tax rate on such income. The recognition date is the date of transfer, as per the general principles of income recognition. The valuation method is derived from Rule 57, which specifies that the fair market value of any other property (including virtual digital assets) is determined by the price it would ordinarily fetch on sale in the open market on the valuation date. TDS is applicable at 1% under s.393(1) for payments to residents. The penalty position is governed by s.439(8), which requires the disclosure of all material facts and a bona fide explanation.
